jobs.title: MBA Technical Strategy and Operations Intern
jobs.description:
Who we are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About the role

We are looking for a graduate student intern with a vehicle or mobility background to support technical strategy and operations for our vehicle engineering team. You will own a defined workstream within one of our programs: the plan, the milestones, the dependencies, the risks, and the weekly readout to engineering leadership. Depending on the workstream, you may also support issue tracking, manufacturing during vehicle builds, and analysis for engineering decisions.

The role is hands-on. Expect regular time in the garage, and on the production floor with the engineers and technicians doing the work.

What you’ll do

- Own the plan for a defined workstream, such as a build, a bench, a supplier transition, a fleet readiness milestone, or a process rollout. Maintain milestones, dependencies, risks, and open actions.

- Publish a weekly status readout to engineering leadership with progress, blockers, decisions needed, and a recommendation for each escalation.

- Keep the issue record current. Prepare the weekly triage, chase owners for updates, and roll the results into the weekly readout.

- Support vehicle builds as needed, including build readiness, parts and kitting status, work instructions, and issue capture on the floor while a build is in progress.

- Pull the quotes, lead times, cost data, and fleet data the program needs, and build the comparisons the engineering owner uses to decide.

- Work with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, fleet operations, and finance to move your workstream forward.

- Identify what is slowing your workstream down, propose a fix, implement it, and measure the result.

What we’re looking for

- Current graduate student in an MBA, an engineering master's (mechanical, electrical, industrial, systems, automotive, or similar), or a related master's program such as engineering management, operations, or supply chain.

- Prior background in vehicles or mobility, including automotive, EV, autonomous vehicles, commercial vehicles, fleet operations, mobility services, off-highway or heavy equipment.

- Comfortable with technical material, including build plans, test reports, and BOMs.

- Experience owning a deliverable through to completion against a schedule.

- Comfortable in a garage and on a production floor.

- Able to commit 15-20 hours per week during the academic term on a consistent schedule, with regular onsite days in San Francisco.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office location. As a company driven by innovation and continuous change, close collaboration is essential. We’re constantly reimagining our industry, creating new products, and refining our processes, and we do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The base starting rate for this role is $56.00 per hour.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

About the Role

Our Payments & Risk Operations team is responsible for the day to day health, reliability, and integrity of our payments platform across the Atoms portfolio, including Otter, CloudKitchens, Picnic, Lab37, and more.

We are looking for someone to own the function end to end across both payments operations and risk operations. From a payments operations perspective, you will own the operational health of pay-ins and payouts, work through processor and merchant issues, identify recurring failure points, and improve payment reliability. Across risk operations, you will own fraud and abuse programs spanning chargebacks, account takeovers, refunds and appeasements, promotional abuse, and emerging threats.

This is a highly hands on, high agency role for someone who is proactive, accountable, and comfortable operating in ambiguity. We are looking for someone who sees an issue, digs into the details, brings the right people together, and drives it through resolution. Whether investigating a merchant escalation, working directly with a processor, analyzing trends in SQL, improving a BPO workflow, or partnering with Product and Engineering on a longer term solution, the right person will bring structure where it is needed, spot gaps early, and continuously raise the bar for how the function operates.

What you’ll do

- Own Payments & Risk Operations end to end. Set the operating agenda, identify where we need to improve, and drive the work forward across both payment operations and risk.

- Own the full risk operations portfolio, including transaction fraud, account takeovers, chargebacks, refunds and appeasements, promotional abuse, KYC/KYB, sanctions related operations, and emerging risk vectors. Continuously evaluate where our controls need to evolve as the business and threat landscape change.

- Serve as the central point of contact for major fraud events and high severity payment or risk escalations, including executive escalations. Take ownership of the response, bring together the right stakeholders, and drive issues through resolution.

- Ability to operate independently and navigate ambiguity with minimal guidance.

- Lead a BPO team responsible for frontline payment and risk operations. Set the team's SOPs, workflows, escalation paths, quality standards, and priorities, and make sure they have the context and tools needed to operate effectively.

- Identify operational pain points before they become recurring problems. Develop a clear point of view on where processes need to change, where tooling is falling short, and where Product and Engineering investment can make the function more scalable.

- Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including Product, Sales, Legal, Customer Success, and Customer Support to drive coordinated risk strategies.

- Own the risk P&L, partnering with Finance and Accounting to report on loss metrics and surface key trends impacting the business.

- Lead red team exercises in collaboration with stakeholders across the company to proactively identify vulnerabilities and stay ahead of emerging risks.

What we’re looking for

- 4-7 years of hands on experience in payments operations, fraud and risk, or financial operations, with meaningful experience across both payments and risk.

- Strong understanding of payment processing and money movement, including pay-ins, payouts, settlement, reconciliation, and processor operations.

- Strong analytical skills, including SQL, with experience using data to identify trends, define KPIs, and drive operational improvements.

- Experience leading or partnering with BPO teams and managing relationships with payment processors, financial partners, and third-party risk vendors.

- High-agency operator with strong cross-functional communication skills, a bias for action, and a proven ability to take ambiguous problems from identification through resolution.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our New York   office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The base salary range for this role is $140,000 - $165,000 per year.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards and an annual performance-based bonus.

Benefits Summary (USA Full-Time Exempt Employees):

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance (multiple plans, incl. HSA options).

jobs.description:

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About the role

Our safety practice is not a document exercise — it is an operating discipline that has to run at the speed of the fleet. This role owns that discipline. You will stand up and run the operational safety machinery: how we manage incidents, how we train and qualify the people in and around our vehicles, how field events get triaged and routed, and how investigations turn into engineering change. Today these functions exist on a smaller scale. Your job is to make them a coherent system that scales as we add vehicles, routes, and customers.

This is a hands-on role. You will write the next version of most of these processes yourself, run the first dozen investigations yourself, and only then hire against the parts that need scale.

What you’ll do

- Incident management:  Own the end-to-end response process: detection, notification, severity classification, on-scene coordination, containment decisions, root cause investigation, corrective action, and closure. Recommend who should have the authority to hold operations and under what conditions, and make sure that authority is real.

- Event triage:  Build the pipeline that turns raw field telemetry, disengagements, operator reports, and near-miss data into a ranked, actionable queue. Set the taxonomy and severity model. Own the triage rate, the backlog, and the time-to-disposition — and make those numbers visible to engineering and leadership.

- Training and qualification:  Design the training and recurrent-qualification program for safety drivers, autonomous vehicle operators, and remote support staff. Own the curriculum, the practical evaluation, and the qualification records.

- Safety data and reporting:  Own the operational safety metrics set and the reporting cadence, and make sure our internal records can withstand outside scrutiny.

- Feedback into engineering:  Be the channel that carries field reality into the product. Partner with the Head of Safety so that operational evidence feeds hazard analysis and change assessment rather than sitting in a separate system.

What we’re looking for

- 6-8+ years in safety operations, fleet safety, transportation safety, or operational risk in a safety-critical domain — commercial trucking, autonomous vehicles, rail, aviation, or industrial operations.

- Demonstrated experience leading real incident investigations to root cause and driving corrective actions to closure. We will ask you to walk through specific investigations in detail.

- Fluency with structured investigation and risk methods — root cause analysis, causal factor charting, human factors analysis, hazard identification — and the judgment to know which one a given event actually warrants.

- Data-driven by default . You are comfortable working directly with event data: querying it, building your own views, and forming a defensible position from it. SQL and basic scripting are expected; you should not need an analyst to tell you what the fleet is doing.

- Working knowledge of the US vehicle regulatory environment, — AV-specific reporting such as the NHTSA Standing General Order, FMCSA regulations, hours of service. Familiarity with SAE J3016 levels and ODD concepts.

- The disposition this work requires: calm under a live incident, rigorous when it would be easier to be reassuring, and willing to be the person who says stop.

- Willingness to be on-site and on-call. Incidents do not respect business hours.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. About the role

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to own hardware issue management for anomalies found during lab testing, on the production floor, and in the field, from intake through verified closure. You’ll run the intake and triage process, own hardware issue tracking in Linear, and keep the record accurate as work progresses. This is a hands-on role based in the garage and test sites, in daily contact with the technicians, test operators, and field engineers who find problems and the engineers who resolve them.

What you’ll do

- Issue Intake: Own all the paths by which a hardware issue reaches engineering, covering the garage, the lab and test benches, vehicles in service, and supplier and incoming inspection findings.

- Issue Tracking in Linear: Own the structure and administration of hardware issue tracking in Linear, including teams and projects, workflow states, label groups, issue templates, intake forms and routing, sub-issue and blocking relationships, and saved views for each audience.

- Triage: Run the daily recurring triage on incoming issues. Set severity and priority, distinguish a one-off issue from potential trends, and assign a named owner, a next action, and a committed date to every open issue.

- Closure: Drive issues through to verified closure with the responsible engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and field teams. Define what evidence closure requires, and reopen an issue as needed.

- Process: Maintain the operating process behind the tracker, including severity and priority definitions, escalation paths, and service levels for triage and closure.

- Reporting: Publish hardware issue status on a fixed cadence, covering open volume and aging, closure rate against inflow, top issues by severity and by frequency, and blocked items with named owners, escalated with a recommendation.

- Automation and Integration: Use Linear's GraphQL API, integrations, and automation rules to reduce manual entry and keep the record current, including Slack intake, status sync, and reporting generated from the tracker.

What we’re looking for

- Bachelor's degree in an engineering or technical field is required, with 6+ years in program management, engineering program management, or a comparable role. Equivalent hands-on experience will be considered in place of the degree.

- Demonstrated ownership of an issue or defect management process end to end, from intake through triage to verified closure, in a hardware or physical product environment.

- Experience administering an issue tracker, including workflow design, taxonomy and label structure, permissions, templates, and reporting views. Linear, Jira, or equivalent.

- Experience migrating a team or organization onto a tracker or internal system, including data migration, cutover, and driving adoption.

- Track record of driving cross-functional issues to closure against committed dates.

- Working knowledge of structured problem solving, including 8D, 5-Why, fishbone, and root cause and corrective action, sufficient to judge whether an investigation is complete.

- Experience working directly with technicians, test operators, or field service teams.

- Demonstrated experience designing an operational process and measuring adherence to it.

- Data fluency sufficient to report on tracker and fleet data directly, in SQL against fleet data and GraphQL or scripting against a tracker API.

- Strong written communication across process documentation, escalations, and status reporting, for technical and executive audiences.

- Ability to work onsite five days a week in San Francisco, with regular time in the garage and some travel to test and deployment sites.

Nice to have

- Hands-on experience configuring and administering Linear, including its API and automation rules.

- Experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive, EV, robotics, aerospace, heavy equipment, or industrial machinery.

- Prior work as an engineer, technician, or operator.

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to own vehicle configuration and change control: the record of what hardware and software is on every R&D vehicle we operate, and the process governing how it changes. In this role, you will define the configuration data model, the capture path that keeps the record accurate against development assets, and the change processes that enable us to test quickly and effectively. Define the configuration data model, including item and revision structure, effectivity rules, and the platform abstractions that hold across differing vehicle types.

- Configuration Capture: Define how configuration data is captured at the point of work, so that build, modification, service, and software update events update the record through the tools technicians and engineers already use. Own record accuracy as a measured metric, including the audit methods used, and the cadence at which it runs.

- Release and Campaign Eligibility: Establish how we determine which properties are eligible for a given software release, test campaign, or data collection mission, and the reason any vehicle is excluded.

- Configuration and Data Provenance: Define how logged data and test results are tied to the configuration that produced them. Partner with software and data teams on how provenance is used in validation and training workflows.

- Enterprise System Requirements: Define configuration requirements for PLM, ERP, MES, and inventory systems, own the integration design between those systems and the configuration record.

- Cross-Functional Ownership: Partner with vehicle integration, manufacturing and technician teams, autonomy and software release, safety, supply chain, and operations, and resolve conflicting requirements across them.

- Working knowledge of software configuration and release management, including version and build identity, update and flashing paths, parameter and calibration management, and fleet-wide version reporting.
